newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Upbeat Dow drives Australian stocks higher at open.
newsitem.headline: Upbeat Dow drives Australian stocks higher at open.

text.p: A bullish Australian stock market bolted higher at the open on Wednesday, taking its lead from a U.S. market that was galvanised by comments from U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan that dispelled concerns about an imminent hike in U.S. interest rates.
Interest rates were the focus locally as well, with hopes high that second quarter inflation data due at 0130 GMT (11,30 a.m.) would prompt a cut in local rates by the Reserve Bank.
The All Ordinaries index jumped 31.3 points to 2,687.7.
"The key thing has been Greenspan's comments and the drive that gave to the equity and bond market in the U.S.," said Phillip Toop, dealer at brokerage Henderson Charlton Jones.
Toop noted the upbeat tone of local bond trading, saying that today's local inflation data was expected to confirm the conditions necessary for another interest rate cut.

"It would take a pretty bad CPI figure to blow this bit of confidence out of the water. Certainly expectations are for confirmation of a low inflation environment which will put a rate cut back on the agenda," he said.

Macquarie Bank shares maintained their upward trajectory after telling the annual meeting that first quarter earnings were well ahead of the same period a year ago. The shares were 30 cents higher at A$13.35 (US$9.88).

The big banks boomed with the bond markets. Commonwealth Bank was most impressive, jumping over 3.5 percent to a record high A$17.00. ANZ Bank, up 2.4 percent and Westpac Banking Corp, up 1.8 percent, were also at record highs of A$10.32 and A$8.12 respectively. Sector heavyweight National Bank was not left out, climbing 1.7 percent to A$19.62.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of more than four to one, while about 33 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
